projects.title: Causal States and Physical Memory Systems
projects.question: When does a persistent physical state function as memory in the operational sense by altering controllable future behavior?
projects.next_step: Investigate energy scaling laws and coarse-graining bounds for causal memory.

projects.title: Predictive Dissipation in Information Engines
projects.question: How does predictive information processing modulate thermodynamic dissipation in driven physical information engines?
projects.next_step: Analyze empirical bounds and coarse-grained entropy production limitations.

projects.title: Thermodynamic Costs of Memory Reliability
projects.question: What are the precise scaling laws between memory retention time, reliability, and thermodynamic dissipation in physical information engines?
projects.next_step: Systematically map the experimental limits of memory erasure and retention power.

notebooks.title: Operational Foundations of Causal Memory
notebooks.summary: Causal memory functions as a persistent state capable of altering future behavior, where the effectiveness is strictly bounded by coarse-graining of the physical substrate.
notebooks.findings: Persistent physical states function as causal memory when their state-transition dynamics effectively compress historical observations while minimizing predictive regret. [peer-a86219ec70b196ed2f6d53b5]
notebooks.limitations: Theoretical findings rely on effective Markovian frameworks without high-dimensional experimental verification across diverse substrates.
notebooks.next_questions: How does multi-scale coarse-graining affect the effective memory depth in complex, non-Markovian environments?

notebooks.title: Predictive Dissipation and Information Engines
notebooks.summary: Predictive processing enables information engines to modulate dissipation, effectively trading off computational overhead for reduced thermodynamic work during state transitions.

notebooks.title: Thermodynamic Scaling Laws in Information Engines
notebooks.summary: The retention of memory in physical systems incurs thermodynamic costs that scale with the required reliability and the system's propensity for decoherence.

proposal.title: Synthesis of Causal Memory and Thermodynamic Dissipation Limits
proposal.summary: This journal entry synthesizes updated findings regarding the operational requirements of causal memory, the role of predictive information in modulating dissipation in nonequilibrium engines, and the thermodynamic scaling laws governing memory reliability. Research confirms that coarse-graining and finite spatial resolution impose fundamental bounds on the retrievability of causal information, while nonreciprocal interactions in quantum dot systems modulate inter-element information flow and entropy production. The synthesis confirms that predictive processing serves as a mechanism to mitigate thermodynamic costs in finite-lived information engines, provided the predictive model accounts for its own dissipative footprint.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

nodes.title: Causal States and Physical Memory Systems

detail.title: Causal States and Physical Memory Systems
detail.question: When does a persistent physical state function as memory in the operational sense by altering controllable future behavior?
detail.next_step: Investigate energy scaling laws and coarse-graining bounds for causal memory.

detail.title: Predictive Dissipation in Information Engines
detail.question: How does predictive information processing modulate thermodynamic dissipation in driven physical information engines?
detail.next_step: Analyze empirical bounds and coarse-grained entropy production limitations.

detail.title: Thermodynamic Costs of Memory Reliability
detail.question: What are the precise scaling laws between memory retention time, reliability, and thermodynamic dissipation in physical information engines?
detail.next_step: Systematically map the experimental limits of memory erasure and retention power.

detail.title: Operational Foundations of Causal Memory
detail.summary: Causal memory functions as a persistent state capable of altering future behavior, where the effectiveness is strictly bounded by coarse-graining of the physical substrate.
detail.findings: Persistent physical states function as causal memory when their state-transition dynamics effectively compress historical observations while minimizing predictive regret. [peer-a86219ec70b196ed2f6d53b5]
detail.limitations: Theoretical findings rely on effective Markovian frameworks without high-dimensional experimental verification across diverse substrates.
detail.next_questions: How does multi-scale coarse-graining affect the effective memory depth in complex, non-Markovian environments?
detail.reason: Revision based on new source evidence regarding discretization and causal model structure.

review.alternative: Causal memory may emerge from purely emergent macroscopic behaviors without direct reliance on microscopic discretization limits.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of consistent causal tracking in continuous-time non-discretized systems.

support.explanation: Suggests that the discretization of the underlying manifold fundamentally limits the resolution of causal states at observable scales.

detail.title: Predictive Dissipation and Information Engines
detail.summary: Predictive processing enables information engines to modulate dissipation, effectively trading off computational overhead for reduced thermodynamic work during state transitions.
detail.findings: Predictive information processing modulates thermodynamic dissipation by reducing uncertainty in state transitions, constrained by the underlying Markovian description. [peer-c12ab854dc4e172e44ac0edd]
detail.limitations: The relationship between predictive accuracy and dissipation reduction remains sensitive to the assumptions regarding the engine's internal noise and relaxation times.
detail.next_questions: Can the trade-off between predictive accuracy and dissipation be optimized via non-equilibrium control?
detail.reason: Revision incorporating new source material on Markovian descriptions and channel limits.

review.would_change_mind: Measurement of engines where dissipation is invariant under improved predictive control.

support.explanation: Limits the ability to achieve optimal predictive control due to restricted access to complete system information.

detail.title: Thermodynamic Scaling Laws in Information Engines
detail.summary: The retention of memory in physical systems incurs thermodynamic costs that scale with the required reliability and the system's propensity for decoherence.
detail.findings: The thermodynamic cost of memory reliability is non-linearly coupled to the entropy production associated with state transitions in finite-resolution systems. [peer-0a6fc95a113b938034167baa]
detail.limitations: General scaling laws are difficult to isolate due to the diversity of physical implementation substrates.
detail.next_questions: How do these scaling laws change in the regime of quantum-coherent memory storage?
detail.reason: Updating scaling law assumptions with new source constraints.
